title: Find files changed recently
body: Use find with a time predicate. For files modified in the last day, run `find . -type f -mtime -1`. Add `-print0` when names may contain spaces and pipe to a command that reads NUL separators.

title: Inspect which process owns a port
body: On Linux, `ss -ltnp` lists listening TCP sockets with process details when permissions allow. `lsof -i :8080` is a portable alternative on systems where lsof is installed.

title: Preserve spaces while iterating over files
body: Avoid parsing `ls`. Emit NUL-delimited paths with `find ... -print0`, then consume them with `while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do ...; done` in a shell that supports the option.

title: Follow service logs with systemd
body: Use `journalctl -u example.service -f` to follow a unit. Add `--since '10 minutes ago'` for a bounded window and `-o short-iso` for timestamps that are easier to compare.

title: Explain disk usage that df and du disagree on
body: A process can keep an unlinked file open. The blocks still count in `df`, while a directory walk by `du` cannot see the deleted name. Check `lsof +L1` and restart or signal the owning process carefully.

title: Send standard error to a file
body: Shell redirections are evaluated left to right. `command >output.log 2>error.log` separates streams. `command >combined.log 2>&1` sends standard error to the same destination already selected for standard output.

title: Count unique lines reliably
body: `uniq` only combines adjacent equal lines, so sort first: `sort input.txt | uniq -c`. For machine-readable output or large pipelines, set a stable locale such as `LC_ALL=C` when bytewise ordering is intended.

title: Stop a command after a time limit
body: GNU `timeout 30s command` sends a termination signal after thirty seconds. Use `--kill-after` to add a later hard-stop window. The exit status distinguishes timeout from many ordinary command failures.

title: Check DNS resolution without ping
body: Use `dig example.com A` or `getent hosts example.com`. Ping tests ICMP reachability and may be blocked even when name resolution and application traffic work normally.

title: Make a shell script fail on pipeline errors
body: In Bash, `set -o pipefail` makes a pipeline return a failure when any component fails, subject to the shell's pipeline rules. Combine options deliberately; `set -e` has contextual exceptions and is not complete error handling.

title: View memory pressure on Linux
body: `free -h` summarizes memory, but available memory is usually more useful than the raw free column because the kernel uses RAM for reclaimable caches. `vmstat 1` can reveal sustained swapping and run-queue pressure.

title: Copy a directory while retaining metadata
body: `rsync -a source/ destination/` recursively copies common metadata and treats the trailing slash as the contents of source. Review ownership requirements and add ACL or extended-attribute options when those are part of the backup contract.

title: Diagnose a command not found error
body:
Check the exact command name and inspect `PATH` with `printf '%s
' "$PATH"`. `command -v tool` shows what the current shell would execute. A newly installed binary may require starting a new shell or correcting permissions.

title: Read a compressed text file without extracting it
body: Use `gzip -cd archive.gz` or `zcat archive.gz` to stream decompressed content to standard output. Pipe that stream into grep, less, or another reader without creating an intermediate file.

title: See environment variables for a process
body: On Linux, `/proc/PID/environ` contains NUL-separated environment entries when permissions permit. Convert separators only for local inspection and avoid logging values because environments commonly contain credentials.

title: Create a secure temporary directory
body: Use `mktemp -d` and retain the returned path. Install a trap that removes that exact validated directory on exit. Do not invent predictable names in a shared temporary location.

title: Compare two directory trees
body: `diff -ru directory-a directory-b` recursively reports textual differences. For synchronization planning, `rsync -ani source/ destination/` provides a dry-run itemized view without writing files.

title: Identify the largest files under a directory
body:
A portable pipeline can emit byte sizes with `find`, then sort numerically. On GNU systems, `find . -type f -printf '%s %p
' | sort -nr | head` is concise, but paths containing newlines require a NUL-aware variant.

title: Run a command when a shell exits
body: A shell trap registers cleanup: `trap cleanup EXIT`. Keep cleanup idempotent because multiple error paths can converge on it, quote resolved paths, and avoid broad recursive deletion targets.

title: Test whether an HTTP service is responding
body: `curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 5 https://service.example/health` reports HTTP errors and bounds the wait. A successful transport check does not by itself prove that dependencies or indexes are ready.
